clue.text: St John's view as he converted sectarian

definitions.note: a noun here: a member of a religious sect

indicators.note: to convert is to change form, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone notes how a man who changed faith sees the Gospel of St John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks like a religious conversion in the surface, but it is the anagram signal for all fifteen letters of ST JOHNS VIEW AS HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Christian denomination are adherents of a distinct sect, hence sectarians.

clue.text: Deer relative heading for tundra still

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
nan is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so the start of tundra is taken

explanation.surface: A reindeer's relative leads the herd toward the motionless tundra.
explanation.definitionFit: Still water is motionless and unmoving, which is what stagnant water is.

clue.text: Find whisky here round bar

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Advice to find your whisky in the round bar of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish west-coast town famous for its single malt distillery, a place to find whisky.

clue.text: Grand love affairs, not right, relatively criminal?

parts.note: grand means big

indicators.note: R, the abbreviation for right, is taken away

parts.note: amours are love affairs

explanation.surface: Grand romances that went wrong are judged somewhat criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively criminal' is a pun: marrying a second spouse is a crime involving relations by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Having two spouses at once is a crime, so a person in that state is criminal in terms of relatives.

clue.text: Female comes in close, one for look

indicators.note: the female letter enters the word for close

parts.note: to close is to shut
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A woman steps in close for a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUFTI is British slang, from Arabic, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance or peek, as in 'take a shufti', is British slang for a look.

clue.text: Uproar as monkey hides duck beneath cape

indicators.note: in a down clue, the monkey part sits below the cape letter

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: the monkey's name holds the duck letter inside it

parts.note: a langur is an Asian monkey
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Noise breaks out as a monkey conceals a duck under its cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a loud, continuous racket, a synonym for uproar.

clue.text: Players notice team's leader training inside

indicators.note: the training letters go within the word for notice

parts.note: to notice is to see
PT is physical training

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Players spot the team captain doing a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven musicians is a septet, so its members are players.

clue.text: With which writer discovers new lead?

definitions.text: With which writer discovers new lead?

parts.words: With which writer discovers new lead?
parts.note: the 'writer' is a pencil and its 'lead' is the graphite core, uncovered fresh by the device

explanation.surface: A writer finds a fresh clue to follow in an investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a journalist or novelist chasing a new lead; the writer is in fact a pencil whose graphite lead is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: This device shaves wood from a pencil so fresh graphite is exposed for writing.

clue.text: Found to be less habit forming?

indicators.note: forming means shaping into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has been shown to be less addictive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find; it is the verb meaning set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, a synonym of establish.

clue.text: True subject and falsehood associated with good English

parts.note: a falsehood is a lie

explanation.surface: A debate on truth and falsehood linked to good English.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege, or liegeman, is a vassal bound to serve a lord faithfully: a loyal subject.

clue.text: Sheer fabrication in South African newspaper?

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical speaking for a group
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A pure invention printed in a South African newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheer fabrication' reads as an outright lie; it means a sheer fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, see-through fabric, so it is a sheer textile.

clue.text: Force clown to entertain American zealot

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take it in, so the clown word holds the American letter

parts.note: an antic is an old word for a clown or buffoon

explanation.surface: Someone forces a clown to amuse an American extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic and a zealot are both people with extreme, uncritical enthusiasm for a cause.

clue.text: Koeman's certainly in an unknown Dutch team

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
Ronald Koeman is a Dutch footballer, and Dutch for yes or certainly is ja
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Koeman is certainly part of an unnamed Dutch football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax of Amsterdam is the most famous football club in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Prone to disturb zho on trail

indicators.note: disturbing letters throws them out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A zho, a yak hybrid, is liable to unsettle walkers on a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: A zho (or dzo) is a Himalayan yak-cattle cross; 'Prone' looks like 'liable', but it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying prone means lying flat, face down, which is a level, lying position.

clue.text: Sun perhaps initially seductive for compilers

parts.note: the sun goes down each evening, so it is something that sets

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A seductive Sun newspaper story aimed at those who compile it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setters are the people who compile puzzles, like Tees who wrote this one.

clue.text: Inspector formerly an underground operative

parts.note: ex means former, formerly
an is the indefinite article, A
a miner works underground

explanation.surface: A police inspector who was once an undercover agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground operative' suggests a resistance spy; it is a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner checks things over closely, which is what an inspector does.

clue.text: Town lad endlessly lacking in refinement

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for lad is dropped

parts.note: a lad is a boy
something unpolished is rough

explanation.surface: A local boy who is forever uncouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own municipal corporation.

clue.text: Row right up close to boat on the rocks

parts.note: a bank is a row, as in a bank of seats
taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Rowing up near a boat that has run aground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' fits the boat scene but means financially ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm on the rocks is in financial ruin, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: The Italian used in one northern location's flawless

parts.note: 'un is northern dialect for one, as in 'a good 'un'

indicators.note: the Italian article is placed inside the word for location

parts.note: a location is a spot
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian placed in a northern spot pronounces it perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoilt is undamaged and in perfect condition, so without any flaw.

clue.text: Tees buys the beers for a song

parts.note: Tees is the setter of this puzzle, so from the setter's view, me
to buy drinks for everyone is to get a round in

explanation.surface: The setter stands everyone a round in exchange for a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' suggests cheaply; it is the definition, a 1964 Beach Boys hit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1964 Beach Boys hit single.

clue.text: Monarch to speak wildly — that's out of place

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
to rant is to speak wildly

explanation.surface: A king raves, which is not proper behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, so wandering out of place.

clue.text: Oscar and Elizabeth taking in small hound

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the name takes the small letter inside

parts.note: Bess is a pet name for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Oscar and Elizabeth adopt a little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hound' looks like a dog; it is the verb meaning to haunt or harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to pursue them relentlessly, as a fixation preoccupies the mind.

clue.text: Employer in old city around southeast

indicators.note: the city name goes around the compass letters

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An employer based in an ancient city near the southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' suggests a boss; here it means one who employs, that is uses, something.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a thing is to use it, so one who employs is a person using it.

clue.text: Bathing beauties tangled in reeds

indicators.note: something tangled is twisted out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swimmers caught up among the reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Nereids are lovely sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus, at home in the water.

clue.text: Food only provided after danger reduced

indicators.note: the word for only comes after the shortened danger word
the word for danger is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a danger is a risk
sole means only

explanation.surface: Food is provided only once the risk has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish, a type of food.

clue.text: Confident Republican in to take action

indicators.note: the party letter goes inside the word for take action

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A self-assured Republican is ready to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure of something means feeling certain and assured about it.

clue.text: Moers in Germany accommodates char

indicators.note: to accommodate is to hold within, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: Moers, a town in Germany, puts up a cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like a charwoman or fish; it is the verb meaning to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to burn slightly on the surface, the same as to scorch lightly.

clue.text: Bond agent smashing luge in crash

parts.note: smashing means excellent, super

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A James Bond spy wrecks a luge sled in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond agent' suggests 007; it means a bonding agent, an adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong instant adhesive is a bonding agent, sticking surfaces firmly together.
